item.title: Iran developing chemical weapons, Israeli defense minister says
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Saudi Arabian authorities said 11 people were injured Tuesday in a strike by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels that hit a tower in Riyadh's Financial District. Yemen's civil war has intensified since the summer, with the Iranian proxy group threatening to choke off oil and gas shipments from Saudi Arabia.Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Iran is developing chemical weapons, and vowed to stop Tehran from obtaining them. Iran has repeatedly denied they are developing chemical weapons.The commander of Iran's army reiterated on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz is closed to all unauthorized traffic and will remain closed until Iran's seven conditions are met, and he appeared to call for Iranian forces to step up their attacks on commercial ships in the vital waterway.

item.title: China launches first foreign astronaut to its space station
item.description:
China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.
Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, is flying alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, 51, and Wu Yi, 39, after the craft blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China on Wednesday morning. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit.
The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program.
Hours earlier, crowds of people attended a send-off ceremony, with many holding up their phones to capture the moment.
Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali of Pakistan and China's Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo wave at a send-off ceremony on Nov. 25, 2026.
Andy Wong/AP Photo
The crew will conduct more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests during their mission, official Chinese news agency Xinhua earlier reported. Ali will conduct a photosynthetic cyanobacteria experiment in orbit during his short-term mission before returning to Earth aboard the Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, it said.
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif offered his best wishes to the astronauts ahead of their mission.
"Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas in its journey to outer space," he said on X on Tuesday.
The joint flight is part of an agreement signed by China and Pakistan in February 2025.
While this was the first spaceflight for Ali and Wu, Tang has flown on two previous missions and is set to become the first astronaut to board the Tiangong space station three times, national broadcaster CCTV said.

item.title: Man on cruise ship goes overboard off Bahamas, search underway
item.description:
Officials are searching for a man who went overboard during a cruise vacation on board Royal Caribbean's Allure of the Seas, according to Bahamian officials.
The Allure of the Seas is on an eight-day Thanksgiving cruise in the Caribbean that departed from Miami on Sunday.
The cruise line called out a passenger's name over the ship's loudspeaker system for several hours before determining that the man had gone overboard, according to passengers on board the cruise ship. The ship then turned around to look for him, the passengers said.
The ship's captain announced Monday that the crew had "received a report of a missing guest" earlier in the day before determining "that the guest had unfortunately gone overboard," according to two recordings of a captain's announcement obtained by CBS News.
Christian Bunse, a passenger aboard the ship, told CBS Miami, "People got quiet when they heard it, because they heard his name again."
Royal Caribbean told CBS News that it "immediately launched a search and rescue effort" to find the man and are working with authorities.
The Coast Guard said the Allure of the Seas alerted it and the Royal Bahamian Defense Force of a man overboard at around 11:30 p.m. on Monday. The Coast Guard said the man was reported to have gone overboard off the coast of San Salvador Island, Bahamas. The Royal Bahamian Defense Force is leading search efforts for the man, aided by the Coast Guard.
An October 2010 file photo of Royal Caribbean's Allure of the Seas.
Roni Lehti/AFP/Getty Images
"We are coordinating with the cruise and will have a vessel on scene," said a spokesperson for the Royal Bahamas Defence Force.

item.title: Armed men take hostages at supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia
item.description:
A group of armed men with their faces covered seized a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena on Tuesday, Colombian police said.
Initially, they were holding around 30 hostages, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. As of Sunday night, they had released 10 of the hostages, including five elderly women, the president and Colombian police said. There was no immediate word on their conditions or the conditions of those still being held.
De la Espriella said that the men were "common criminals" who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck.
The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets, which has recently spread to urban areas.
Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of an Exito supermarket in Cartagena's La Castellana neighborhood, while local media have broadcast images of snipers on nearby buildings in what appears to be a standoff between the armed men and police.
Soldiers stand guard outside a supermarket where armed men are holding hostages, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella, in Cartagena, Colombia, Nov. 24, 2026.
AP Photo/Jose Manuel Pedraza
Cartagena is one of Colombia's main tourist destinations. The city of a million people is famous for its well-preserved 18th-century architecture and the thick stone walls built to defend it from pirate attacks.
Cartagena's airport temporarily suspended its operations on Tuesday following the incident. But it later said in a social media post that operations were slowly returning to normal.

item.title: Top Denmark court upholds "non-Western" evictions law
item.description:
Denmark's Supreme Court upheld on Monday a controversial law intended to eliminate ethnic enclaves in public housing, or "ghettos," as the government calls them, by giving authorities the ability to limit the number of "non-Western" immigrants and their descendants who can live in any particular housing development.
The court ruled that the eviction in 2022 of residents from Nøjsomhed-Sydvej, a housing development in the city of Helsingør, north of Copenhagen, did not constitute ethnic discrimination.
The Danish law introduced in 2018 is among Europe's most aggressive attempts to force immigrant communities to assimilate and to avoid the evolution of "parallel societies" in the country. It has attracted both international condemnation and admiration from politicians in other countries that seek to emulate Denmark's approach to immigration and integration.
Under the legislation, residential areas with at least 1,000 inhabitants, where more than 50% of residents are immigrants or descendants of immigrants from "non-Western" countries, and which meet certain socioeconomic criteria relating to employment rates, income levels, education attainment, and crime, can be subject to redevelopment requirements.
Housing developments designated as "transformation areas" are required to reduce the proportion of public family housing to no more than 40% by 2030. This can involve demolishing buildings, selling properties to private landlords, or converting them to other forms of housing, resulting in the eviction and relocation of some residents.
Under the law, non-Western countries include all nations outside the European Union, Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Vatican State, the U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand. item.title: Iranian women praise singer lashed for not wearing a hijab
item.description:
Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed 74 times on Monday after being convicted of the crime of "outraging public decency" for performing without the head covering that is mandatory for women in the country.
Ahmadi was dealt the corporal punishment for her chosen attire during a livestreamed concert in 2024, according to her attorney, who was quoted by the reformist Iranian newspaper Etemad on Monday. But Iranian women who spoke with CBS News on Tuesday said she was punished not for breaking the rule, but for daring to publicly defy the country's repressive regime — defiance that has made her "a symbol of resistance."
Ahmadi's lawyer told Etemad that the singer and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in the holy city of Qom, as required after their sentences were upheld in September by a local criminal court.
Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed 74 times by Iranian authorities for "outraging public decency" by singing without her hair covered, as required by Iranian dress code rules for women, in a livestreamed 2024 concert.
Parastoo Ahmadi/YouTube
The court in Qom upheld the convictions for "outraging public decency," citing "immoral" content posted online during Ahmadi's performance in December 2024, which went viral in Iran.
In addition to the 74 lashes, Ahmadi and eight members of her team were also sentenced to a two-year ban on travel out of the country and a two-year ban on all "artistic activity."
